data.title: CryptoQuant Says Bitcoin Must Clear $81,700 to Confirm New Bull Market
data.description:
CryptoQuant said bitcoin needs to break above $81,700 to confirm that a new bull market is underway. According to NS3.AI, the asset’s 24% rally over two weeks has stalled as it has traded between $76,000 and $82,000.

CryptoQuant said bitcoin may find support at $70,000 if it weakens further. The firm also identified a lower support zone between $62,000 and $65,000 if the price falls more sharply.

data.title: Thailand Proposes Stablecoin Transfer Rule With 5 Million Baht Daily Cap
data.description: Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed a stablecoin transfer rule that would require customers to use wallets verified as their own. According to NS3.AI, the rule would prohibit deposits from another person's account and withdrawals to another person's account through supervised operators. Transfers would be capped at 5 million baht per day per person per operator.

data.title: Bitcoin Suisse Plans to Cut Up to 60 Jobs in Switzerland
data.description:
Bitcoin Suisse plans to cut up to 60 jobs in Switzerland, affecting about half of its Swiss workforce. According to NS3.AI, the company is also closing its IT development site in Copenhagen.

CEO Andrej Majcen said the restructuring is intended to support international growth and is not linked to difficult crypto market conditions.

data.title: ECB’s Lagarde Says Inflation Shock Will Persist Longer
data.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said euro-area inflation will stay elevated for some time, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Tesla Sets Oct. 1 Event for Next-Generation Roadster
data.description: Tesla Inc. teased an Oct. 1 event to showcase its next-generation Roadster, according to Bloomberg. CEO Elon Musk first unveiled the niche vehicle in November 2017.

data.title: U.S. No Longer the Default Choice for Weapons Purchases and Fund Storage, Axios Reports
data.description: According to Jin10, Axios reported that the United States is gradually no longer the default choice for other governments to buy weapons and store funds, and it has also lost appeal for foreign students.

data.title: Dayana Yastremska Says Family Apartment Destroyed In Odesa Strike
data.description: According to the BBC, Ukrainian tennis player Dayana Yastremska said her family's apartment was destroyed in a Russian aerial strike on the Black Sea port of Odesa. She said the flat was hit by a Kalibr cruise missile, while Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper said 37 people were injured, including a baby, and two people were missing after missile and drone attacks on Odesa and nearby Chornomorsk on Friday night. Yastremska, who reached the semifinals of the Australian Open in 2024 and is ranked 113th in the women's world singles rankings, also posted images of the wreckage on social media and said only a Roland Garros towel survived.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Warsh in Focus as G7 Central Banks Face Rate-Hike Pressure
data.description:
Central banks across much of the Group of Seven face a pivotal week as rising inflation risks increase pressure to raise interest rates, according to Bloomberg.

The report centers on Warsh as policymakers confront the prospect of tighter policy.

data.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde Says European Economy Is Resilient
data.description: According to Jin10, ECB President Christine Lagarde said the European economy is resilient, and that the current inflation shock will last longer, while market volatility and pressure from energy prices are expected to continue.

data.title: Skimpflation Warning as Tinned Mackerel Alternative Hits More Supermarket Shelves
data.description:
Which? has warned that supermarkets selling jack mackerel instead of Atlantic mackerel is an example of “skimpflation”, as Princes and Lidl expand use of the cheaper fish, according to BBC. Princes said last October it was changing all of its tinned mackerel products to jack mackerel, while Lidl is selling the fish under its house brand.

The consumer group said shoppers may be paying the same price for a product with less nutritional value. Jack mackerel has about half as much omega-3 and around a third as much vitamin B12 as traditional mackerel. Princes said its products are clearly identified and were introduced after product and consumer testing, describing jack mackerel as having a milder flavour and meatier texture.

The switch comes as Atlantic mackerel stocks have fallen sharply after years of overfishing. The Marine Stewardship Council says catches in the north-east Atlantic have exceeded scientific advice by an average of 39% over the past 15 years, while Ices says stocks have dropped by roughly three-quarters over the past decade and has advised cutting 2026 catches by about 70%.

data.title: Judge Rules Trump Administration Broke Law In FEMA Workforce Cuts
data.description:
According to CNBC, a U.S. judge ruled that the Trump administration broke the law by ordering the Federal Emergency Management Agency to cut its workforce in half. U.S. District Judge Susan Illston in San Francisco said the Department of Homeland Security unlawfully usurped FEMA's authority over its own personnel and directed the agency to cut thousands of disaster-response jobs. Illston said the department violated a federal law adopted after Hurricane Katrina in 2005 when it moved last year to stop FEMA from renewing the temporary contracts of thousands of on-call reservists who respond to disasters.

Friday's ruling did not include remedies or penalties. Illston said those issues would be addressed in a separate ruling next month, and the parties may submit briefings on the scope of relief she should provide to the unions. FEMA and DHS did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Saturday. Democracy Forward, which represents the plaintiffs, praised the ruling. Skye Perryman, the group's president and CEO, said Congress created FEMA to operate independently because of its mission to prepare and respond quickly when disasters arise. Illston also said FEMA projected staffing for the upcoming fiscal year at 11,383 employees, or about half of prior levels, without any basis for choosing that number.

data.title: Trezor Says ShipMonk Breach Affected 80,689 US Customers
data.description: Trezor said approximately 67,000 additional US customers were affected by a ShipMonk breach, bringing the total to 80,689 affected customers. According to NS3.AI, the exposed information included contact and delivery details, while Trezor said its systems, devices, and parcel contents were not affected.

data.title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Won't Go Public This Year
data.description: According to Axios, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview released Saturday that the company will not go public this year because it still has significant safety work to do. Altman said it would be an ill-advised time to pursue an IPO and added, "I would say not 2026, yeah. We got a lot of stuff to do."

data.title: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Pushed for F-15 Airmen to Join '60 Minutes' Interview After Iran Shootdown
data.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and political appointees pushed for the two F-15 airmen whose plane was shot down over Iran in April to take part in a '60 Minutes' interview, according to multiple sources. CNN Breaking News posted on X, citing several sources familiar with the matter, said the effort involved senior political appointees.

The report said the push centered on the airmen involved in the April incident over Iran, though no further details were provided about whether the interview took place or what the airmen were asked to discuss.

data.title: Nidec To Withdraw From Cambodia Production Amid Thailand Border Dispute
data.description: According to Nikkei Asia, Japanese motor maker Nidec will withdraw from production in Cambodia because of the impact of the border dispute with Thailand. The company is pulling back from the country as the dispute affects its operations.

data.title: Ripple Executive Says Corporate Treasuries Are Key Growth Opportunity for RLUSD
data.description:
Ripple Stablecoin Senior Vice President Jack McDonald said corporate treasuries are an important growth opportunity for RLUSD. According to Odaily, Ripple Treasury serves about 1,200 corporate treasury and CFO clients after Ripple acquired treasury management software provider GTreasury for $1 billion last year, and those clients handle about $13 trillion in transactions annually.

McDonald said RLUSD circulating supply has grown more than 50% over the past month, with about $1 billion on XRP Ledger and $1.4 billion on Ethereum. He added that RLUSD daily active volume has more than doubled since the start of the year, rising from about $200 million last month to about $750 million. Payments and capital markets are currently the two main use cases, and Ripple has worked with Franklin Templeton and DBS on tokenized money market funds and lending.

data.title: Cardano Launches Hydra 2.4.1 as Stablecoin Supply Hits Record $68.2 Million
data.description: Cardano developers launched the Hydra 2.4.1 upgrade with a focus on network security. According to NS3.AI, Cardano's stablecoin supply reached a record $68.2 million after rising from a year-to-date low of $36 million. ADA was trading at $0.2080, up 53% from its lowest level this year, while Cardano's total value locked fell to $54 million, its lowest level since 2023.
